risks.title: Persistent and Broadening Inflationary Pressures
risks.summary: Inflation remains elevated and shows signs of broadening beyond initial drivers, posing a challenge to central bank mandates and potentially requiring further restrictive monetary policy.
risks.watch_for: Core PCE inflation readings, Federal Reserve statements on inflation outlook and policy stance.
sources: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia (Economic Outlook, November 2026)

risks.title: Geopolitical Escalation and Commodity Price Volatility
risks.summary: Escalating geopolitical conflicts, particularly in the Middle East, are driving energy price spikes and commodity market disruptions, contributing to inflation and policy uncertainty.
risks.watch_for: Developments in the Middle East conflict, energy price trends, World Bank commodity price forecasts.
sources: World Bank (Commodity Prices Set to Increase, October 2026)

risks.title: AI Investment Boom and Potential Narrative Shift
risks.summary: Significant investment in Artificial Intelligence is fueling economic growth and productivity, but a reassessment of AI expectations or a failure to deliver on promised returns could lead to market volatility.
risks.watch_for: Corporate earnings from AI-related sectors, market sentiment shifts regarding AI, Federal Reserve's monitoring of AI expectations.
sources: Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch)

risks.title: Fiscal Vulnerabilities and Rising Debt Levels
risks.summary: Persistent large budget deficits and rising national debt levels pose a long-term risk to fiscal sustainability and could constrain policy options.
risks.watch_for: Congressional Budget Office (CBO) deficit and debt projections, government spending and revenue trends.
sources: Congressional Budget Office (Budget and Economic Outlook, February 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch)

risks.title: Fragmented Global Economy and Trade Tensions
risks.summary: Increasing geopolitical fragmentation and persistent trade tensions create uncertainty and could disrupt global supply chains and economic activity.
risks.watch_for: New trade policy announcements, geopolitical developments impacting trade routes, IMF and World Bank assessments of trade risks.

risks.title: Labor Market Resilience Amid Slowing Growth
risks.summary: While the labor market has shown resilience, a slowdown in job growth and a 'low-hire, low-fire' equilibrium could leave the economy vulnerable to shocks.
risks.watch_for: Monthly employment reports (nonfarm payrolls, unemployment rate), wage growth data, Federal Reserve's assessment of labor market conditions.
sources: Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch)

risks.title: Consumer Affordability Challenges
risks.summary: Consumers face headwinds from elevated energy prices and cooling wage growth, impacting purchasing power and potentially dampening overall economic activity.
risks.watch_for: Consumer price index (CPI) and personal consumption expenditures (PCE) data, retail sales figures, consumer sentiment surveys.
sources: Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch)

risks.title: Policy Uncertainty and Monetary Policy Stance
risks.summary: Uncertainty surrounding future monetary policy decisions, including potential further rate hikes, creates volatility and impacts investment decisions.
risks.watch_for: Federal Reserve FOMC statements and meeting minutes, Federal Reserve officials' speeches, market pricing of future interest rate moves.

consensus_note: There is a broad consensus across institutions regarding the persistent nature of inflation and the significant downside risks posed by geopolitical tensions and their impact on commodity prices. While AI is seen as a growth driver, there's a shared concern about its sustainability and potential for market volatility. Fiscal sustainability and rising debt levels are also flagged as significant long-term risks. Divergence appears in the precise timing and magnitude of inflation's decline and the ultimate path of monetary policy.
